data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"No single protocol is intrinsically safest; rather, safety is the comparative latency invariant that seal-visibility latency must be bounded above by failure-detection latency, and the exact durable record must be the pair of causal timestamps (seal-emission, death-detection) together with their happens-before proof.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Clock skew or partition makes the latency order unobservable, reducing the meta-criterion to a vacuous check.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The partial-order proof itself can be lost during a reclaimer crash, creating a second-order displacement risk.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The model assumes asynchronous message passing; if the network is synchronous, the criterion collapses to simple timeout ordering and loses discriminative power.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Adjudication between log-based and lease-based rivals proceeds by measuring worst-case seal-visibility latency under asynchrony. The protocol whose seal can be observed by the reclaimer strictly before the reclaimer concludes death is safe. The durable record must therefore include a vector clock or hybrid logical clock establishing that the seal event precedes the reclamation event in the happens-before relation, making the safety property verifiable from the record alone.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
